text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Kulikov, saying there were more than 8,000 crimininal groups in his country, said on Friday Russia wanted to create an Interpol-type organisation for the ex-Soviet Union.

"We want to create, with Interpol's aide, a network for police cooperation aligned on the structure of the former Soviet Union," Kulikov, who is also Interior Minister, told reporters during a visit to Interpol's world headquarters in this central France city.
Interpol is a liaison group between police forces and uses its extensive communications system to distribute information between police around the world.
Kulikov said that despite a 250 percent increase in economic crimes between 1993 and 1996 and 5,000 corruption cases, "it would be wrong to speak of the existence of an actual Mafia in Russia.

"Organised crime is widespread but it concerns a great many groups which are each small-sized. In time, of course the big ones could swallow up the small ones and there could be some really big organisations but that is not the case today," he said.

A U.S. study in the World Bank newsletter Transition, published last month, showed that nearly half the Russian economy was controlled by organised crime, known as the mafia after Italy's gangs, and billions of dollars were haemorrhaging out of Russia as a result.
